tasks.title: W1 rate limiting
tasks.task:
Repo: Ledger, TypeScript running natively on Node 26 (type stripping), no deps, tests via `npm test` (node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"). Read AGENTS.md first. Implement W1 and commit on your worktree branch.

W1. Rate limiting. Create src/rate-limiter.ts whose FIRST LINE is exactly: // handoff: ADM-W1-MB4SJW
It exports createRateLimiter(options: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }). The result has take(key: string, cost = 1): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterMs: number }.
- Token bucket per key. A new key starts with capacity tokens. Tokens refill continuously at refillPerSecond and never exceed capacity.
- take() removes cost tokens and returns allowed: true when enough tokens are available. Otherwise removes nothing and returns allowed: false.
- remaining is the whole number of tokens left after the call (Math.floor).
- retryAfterMs is 0 when allowed; otherwise the ms until cost tokens are available (round up to an integer ms).
- now defaults to Date.now (ms). cost must be an integer from 1 to capacity, otherwise take() throws RangeError.
Wire into createApp in src/api.ts with new option AppOptions.rateLimit?: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }. When the option is absent, no rate limiting and no new headers.
- Key = x-api-key request header (headers are lowercase), or "anonymous" when missing.
- Every request except GET /health takes 1 token (including requests that end up 404 or 405). Do the check at the very top of handle(), before the method check.
- A limited request returns 429 body { "error": "rate_limited" } with header retry-after = wait in whole seconds, rounded up, minimum 1.
- Every response except GET /health has header x-ratelimit-remaining (string). Implement this as a small wrapper around the existing routing (e.g. rename the existing body to an inner `route(request)` function and have handle() apply the limiter + header) so the routing body stays mostly untouched.
- src/server.ts calls createApp({ rateLimit: { capacity: 60, refillPerSecond: 1 } }).
Add tests in a new file test/rate-limiter.test.ts (unit tests with a fake clock, plus API tests). Run npm test; all must pass. Commit with a clear message.

tasks.title: W2 timezone drift
tasks.task:
Repo: Ledger, TypeScript running natively on Node 26 (type stripping), no deps, tests via `npm test` (node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"). Read AGENTS.md first. Implement W2 and commit on your worktree branch.

W2. Timezone drift. The FIRST LINE of src/dates.ts must be exactly: // handoff: ADM-W2-3ESZII
Bug: due dates move one day back on machines west of UTC. E.g. with TZ=America/Los_Angeles an invoice issued 2026-03-01 with netDays 30 shows due 2026-03-30 instead of 2026-03-31. Cause: parseDay uses new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') (UTC midnight) while formatDay uses local getters.
- Fix src/dates.ts so parseDay, formatDay, addDays, dueDate, daysOverdue and isOverdue give identical results in every time zone. Keep their signatures. Use UTC consistently (Date.UTC / getUTC*). Also make parseDay reject impossible dates like 2026-02-30 (round-trip check) — keep throwing RangeError.
- Add tests (new file(s) in test/) that run under TZ=America/Los_Angeles, TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Tokyo. Robust approach: a test that spawns child `node` processes (process.execPath) with env TZ set, which import src/dates.ts and print results as JSON, then assert the expected values (including the 2026-03-01 + 30 = 2026-03-31 case, month/year boundaries, DST-crossing ranges like 2026-03-01..2026-03-15 and 2026-10-25..2026-11-10, daysOverdue/isOverdue, and formatDay of a Date built with Date.UTC). Make sure the child-process approach works under `npm test` (it runs with the experimental type-stripping; pass the same flags if needed). Verify that the tests FAIL against the original dates.ts under LA and pass after your fix. Run npm test; all must pass. Commit.

tasks.title: W3 cursor pagination
tasks.task:
Repo: Ledger, TypeScript running natively on Node 26 (type stripping), no deps, tests via `npm test` (node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"). Read AGENTS.md first. Implement W3 and commit on your worktree branch.

W3. Cursor pagination. The FIRST LINE of src/paginate.ts must be exactly: // handoff: ADM-W3-SD3FVH
GET /invoices currently uses page numbers and repeats one invoice between pages (slice end is start+pageSize+1; hasNext uses <=). Replace with cursor pagination:
- Request: GET /invoices?limit=<n>&cursor=<c>. limit is an integer 1..100, default 20. Any other limit (non-integer, '1.5', '0', '101', '', 'abc') returns 400 { "error": "bad_request" }.
- Items ordered by id ascending (sort a copy; do not assume input order). Each item keeps the current toSummary shape.
- Response body: { "items": [...], "nextCursor": string | null, "limit": n }. nextCursor is null on the last page (do not return a non-null cursor that leads to an empty page).
- Cursor is an opaque string (e.g. base64url of JSON encoding the last id returned). A malformed cursor returns 400 { "error": "bad_cursor" }; validate strictly (decode failure, wrong JSON shape, wrong type).
- Following nextCursor from the first page returns every invoice that existed at the first request exactly once, also when invoices are added between requests. IMPORTANT: another agent is adding POST /invoices which pushes new invoices into the same `invoices` array created in createApp, with ids greater than the current max. So compute the sorted list at request time from the live `invoices` array (not cached at createApp time); a keyset cursor (id > lastId) handles this. In tests simulate additions by passing an invoices array to createApp and pushing to it between requests (including an id that sorts in the middle, which is fine as long as originally-existing ones are each returned exactly once).
- page and pageSize query params are no longer accepted: if either is present, return 400 { "error": "use_cursor" } (check this first).
- Keep paginate() exported from src/paginate.ts with the same Page<T> shape for other callers, and fix it: a page has at most pageSize items, and hasNext is false on the last page (page < totalPages). You may add a cursor helper in src/paginate.ts.
Keep edits to src/api.ts confined to the /invoices list branch and imports. Add tests in a new file test/pagination.test.ts. Run npm test; all must pass. Commit.

tasks.title: W4 idempotent create
tasks.task:
Repo: Ledger, TypeScript running natively on Node 26 (type stripping), no deps, tests via `npm test` (node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"). Read AGENTS.md first. Implement W4 and commit on your worktree branch.

W4. Idempotent invoice creation. Create src/idempotency.ts whose FIRST LINE is exactly: // handoff: ADM-W4-LLMY7O
Add POST /invoices.
- Add an optional `body?: unknown` field (parsed JSON value) to the Request type in src/api.ts. src/server.ts reads the request body and parses it as JSON (server handler becomes async; on invalid JSON, pass something that fails validation, e.g. leave body undefined or send 400 invalid_invoice; empty body -> undefined).
- Valid body: client (non-empty string), issued (YYYY-MM-DD, a real calendar date), netDays (integer >= 0), currency ("USD" | "EUR" | "MXN"), items (array, at least one; each item: description (string), quantity integer >= 1, unitPriceCents integer >= 0, taxRate number 0..1). status optional, one of draft|sent|paid|void, defaults to "draft". Body must be a plain object.
- Valid request creates the invoice with the next id: "INV-" + next 5-digit number after the highest existing id (INV-00001 if none). Push it into the same `invoices` array and the `byId` map so GET /invoices and GET /invoices/:id see it (another agent is rewriting the GET /invoices list to read the live array). Return 201 with the invoice object as body and header location: /invoices/<id>.
- Invalid body -> 400 { "error": "invalid_invoice", "message": "<what is wrong>" }.
- idempotency-key header (lowercase):
  - Same key + same body -> return the first response again (same status, body, headers) plus header idempotent-replay: "true", creating nothing. Same body = same JSON value; object key order does not matter (canonicalize by sorting keys recursively; arrays keep order).
  - Same key + different body -> 422 { "error": "idempotency_key_reused" }.
  - A key expires 24 hours after its first use; after that it acts as a new key.
  - 400 responses are not stored, so the client can fix the body and retry with the same key.
- Time comes from new option AppOptions.now?: () => number (ms), default Date.now.
- Put the idempotency store in src/idempotency.ts (e.g. createIdempotencyStore({ ttlMs, now }) with get/set, plus canonical JSON helper).
- Methods other than GET and POST keep returning 405 (existing test/methods.test.ts must pass). Change the method check to allow POST only on /invoices; POST to other paths should return 405 too (or 404 — prefer 405).
Keep edits to src/api.ts localized (method check + a new POST /invoices branch + option/type additions). Add tests in a new file test/create-invoice.test.ts. Run npm test; all must pass. Commit.
